newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-TSHWETE MEETS MANDELA IN RUGBY TALKS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TSHWETE MEETS MANDELA IN RUGBY TALKS.

text.p: South Africa's Sports Minister Steve Tshwete met President Nelson Mandela on Tuesday to ask for the five-month-old investigation into the running of rugby union in the republic to be given legal powers.
But a spokesperson said after the meeting that no announcement would be made until after Tshwete had met the five-man task force on Wednesday.

The minister asked for the probe to become the subject of a full-blown commission of inquiry in response to rugby bosses ordering their officials not to co-operate with the original investigation which was appointed to examine everything from allegations of financial misdealings to racism.
The South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) believes the task force was working outside the agreed terms of reference and have said they will fight any upgrading.
"If the inquiry is granted by President Mandela we will apply to have it negated in court," SARFU president Louis Luyt said in a statement.
